notes:
Summary: LumenPrompt builds a VS Code extension used by ~7k devs (in beta). Key ask: sub-100ms inline suggestions for short completions and streaming token-by-token playback for large completions. They care about model/version pinning so users can opt into different model channels (stable/beta/experimental) and for reproducible snippets.

POC scope: 3-day perf run against 5000 sample completions (avg prompt 80 tokens, completion 40 tokens) with real-world concurrency (30 concurrent editors). Metrics: p50/p90 latency for first token, sustain throughput, percent of degraded fallback flows.

Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO for enterprise customers (SAML), audit logging for edits and inference, KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Data residency question for EU customers -> likely Dedicated/Private.

Rate limiting: extension has freemium tier; worry that power users will hit token-based limits and get poor UX. Want guidance on per-editor rate limits and graceful 429 -> fallback to local cached suggestions.

Quotes: "We need inline completions to feel instant — even a 100ms jitter is noticeable to power users." — CTO Rajeev Kapoor.

Open items: KMS integration doc, sample SLA for Dedicated, pricing scenarios for 50k monthly active devs. AE follow-up: send technical runbook + perf test harness (by 2024-11-25).
summary: Mid-market VS Code copilot vendor evaluating Redwood for hosted/dedicated inference. Focus: streaming completions, low-latency inline suggestions, model pinning, KMS and SSO. Near-term POC and procurement in next quarter.
